literal: Deposed Crown Prince; Prince of Jingzhao; Prince of Qinghe; Prince of Guangping; Prince of Runan
idiomatic: The Deposed Crown Prince; the Prince of Jingzhao; the Prince of Qinghe; the Prince of Guangping; the Prince of Runan

literal: Emperor Xiaowen seven sons.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen had seven sons.

literal: The Lin Empress bore the deposed crown prince Xun.
idiomatic: The Lin Empress bore Xun, who would become the deposed crown prince.

literal: Empress Wen Zhao bore Emperor Xuanwu and Prince of Guangping, posthumous name Huai.
idiomatic: Empress Wen Zhao bore Emperor Xuanwu and Huai, Prince of Guangping.

literal: [2] Consort Yuan gave birth to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
idiomatic: [2] Consort Yuan bore Yu, Prince of Jingzhao.

literal: Lady Luo gave birth to Prince of Qinghe, posthumous Wenxian Yi, and Prince of Runan, posthumous Wenzuan Yue.
idiomatic: Lady Luo bore Yi, Prince of Qinghe (posthumous Wenxian), and Yue, Prince of Runan (posthumous Wenzuan).

literal: Zheng Chonghua bore the prince Ti; he was not enfeoffed and died young.
idiomatic: Zheng Chonghua bore the prince Ti, who was never enfeoffed and died in infancy.

literal: The Deposed Crown Prince, the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.
idiomatic: The Deposed Crown Prince Xun, reduced to commoner rank, styled Yuandao.

literal: At birth his mother died; Empress Dowager Wenming raised and watched over him, always keeping him at her side.
idiomatic: His mother died when he was born; Empress Dowager Wenming reared him and kept him constantly at her side.

literal: At age four the Grand Empress Dowager personally established his name Xun, styled Yuandao, and thereupon a general amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: When he was four the Grand Empress Dowager herself named him Xun, styled Yuandao, and a general amnesty was declared.

literal: [3] In the seventh month of Taihe year seventeen, on day guichou, Xun was installed as crown prince.
idiomatic: [3] In the seventh month of Taihe year 17, on the day guichou, Xun was installed as crown prince.

literal: At his capping in the ancestral temple Gaozu sat in the east hall of the Guangji Palace, drew Xun in to see him, and admonished him on the meaning of the cap, saying: "The capping rite manifests itself to a hundred generations; by it one sets the body right, aligns the complexion, and orders one's speech.
idiomatic: When Xun was capped in the ancestral temple, Gaozu received him in the east hall of the Guangji Palace and taught him the meaning of the ceremony: "The capping rite stands for a hundred generations. It sets the body upright, aligns the face, and orders the tongue."

literal: When the body is right, the complexion aligned, and speech in order;
idiomatic: When bearing is upright, the face composed, and words measured,

literal: then lord and minister can be set right, father and son drawn close, elder and younger harmonized.
idiomatic: then ruler and minister are set right, father and son brought near, and elder and younger brought into harmony.

literal: Yet when he sees his mother he must bow, to his brothers he must show respect—charged with the rites of a grown man.
idiomatic: Yet he must bow when he sees his mother and show respect to his brothers, for he is now bound by the rites of adulthood.

literal: Your style is Ru Yuandao; what is entrusted to you is not light.
idiomatic: Your style is Ru Yuandao—what is laid upon you is no small thing.

literal: You should seek the meaning in your name and follow my intent.
idiomatic: Seek the meaning in your name and walk in accord with my intent."

literal: " In year twenty his style was changed to Xuandao.
idiomatic: In year 20 his style was changed to Xuandao.

literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict ordered Xun to proceed to the Dai capital.
idiomatic: When the court moved to Luoyang, Xun was ordered to go to the Dai capital.

literal: His comings and goings and ritual deportment Gaozu fixed for him in every detail.
idiomatic: Gaozu prescribed every detail of his movements and ceremonial bearing.

literal: When Xun entered to take leave Gaozu said: "Now you should not go toward Dai; but the Grand Preceptor has died at Hengrang. I, having taken up the weight of the imperial pole, cannot lightly go to my maternal uncle's mourning. I wish you to extend mourning for your maternal uncle and bow at your mother's tomb, writing out in full a son's feeling.
idiomatic: When Xun came to take leave Gaozu said, "You are not to turn toward Dai. The Grand Preceptor has died at Hengrang. I bear the weight of the throne and cannot lightly attend my uncle's mourning. Go and mourn for him in my stead, bow at your mother's tomb, and pour out there everything a son owes."

literal: When you arrive there, one day after the Grand Preceptor's rites are finished you should once bow at the mountain tomb.
idiomatic: "When you arrive, wait one day after the Grand Preceptor's rites are done, then bow once at the imperial tombs."

literal: When the bowing is finished your clan-grandfather the Prince of Nan'an may once be approached for inquiry.
idiomatic: "After that you may call once on your clan-grandfather, the Prince of Nan'an."

literal: On the road you should diligently read the classics.
idiomatic: "On the road, read the classics with steady care."

literal: Today you see me in person.
idiomatic: "Today you see me face to face."

literal: " [4] Afterward, whenever Gaozu went on campaign each year, Xun always remained to guard the capital and preside over temple sacrifices.
idiomatic: [4] Thereafter, whenever Gaozu marched out each year, Xun stayed behind to guard the capital and preside over the ancestral rites.

literal: Xun did not love literary study; his body was large and fat; he deeply dreaded the heat of the He-Luo region; his mind always yearned for the pleasures of the north.
idiomatic: Xun cared little for books. He was heavy of build and loathed the heat of the He-Luo basin; his heart always turned northward.

literal: The household steward Gao Daoyue repeatedly spoke bitter admonition; Xun greatly harbored resentment.
idiomatic: His household steward Gao Daoyue admonished him again and again until Xun came to hate him.

literal: When Gaozu visited Mount Song, Xun guarded Jinyong; within the west side gate he plotted with his attendants to summon the horse-tenders' light cavalry and flee to Dai, and with his own hand cut down Daoyue in the forbidden precinct.
idiomatic: While Gaozu was at Mount Song, Xun held Jinyong. Inside the west side gate he plotted with his attendants to call up the horse-keepers' light cavalry and flee to Dai, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the inner palace.

literal: The commandant of guards Yuan Yan restrained the gates; by night all was quiet.
idiomatic: The commandant of guards Yuan Yan barred the gates and held the night quiet.

literal: At dawn Director of Documents Lu Diu hurried a memorial to Gaozu in the south; Gaozu, hearing it, was alarmed and grieved; outwardly he concealed the matter and still went as far as Bian mouth before returning.
idiomatic: At dawn Director of Documents Lu Diu sent an urgent report south. Gaozu was shaken and grieved, but outwardly he hid the affair and still rode as far as Bian mouth before turning back.

literal: He drew out Xun's many crimes; with the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally caned Xun, and ordered Xi and the others to take turns—more than a hundred blows—and had him dragged out; for more than a month he could not rise.
idiomatic: He recited Xun's crimes one by one. With the Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally beat him, then had them take turns until more than a hundred strokes were laid on. Xun was dragged out and could not rise for over a month.

literal: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.
idiomatic: He was confined in a lodge apart, west of the city.

literal: Gaozu summoned the ministers at the Clear Emblem Hall and discussed deposing him.
idiomatic: Gaozu summoned the ministers to the Clear Emblem Hall to discuss deposing him.

literal: Director of Works and Crown Prince Grand Tutor Mu Liang, and Vice Director and Junior Tutor Li Chong, both removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.
idiomatic: Director of Works and crown prince grand tutor Mu Liang, and vice director and junior tutor Li Chong, both removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.

literal: Gaozu said: "What you apologize for is private; what I discuss is the state.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "What you apologize for is a private matter. What I discuss is the state."

literal: The ancients had a saying: great righteousness extinguishes kin.
idiomatic: "The ancients said that great righteousness may destroy one's own kin."

literal: Now Xun wishes to oppose his father, turn from his superior, seize and hold Heng and Shuo.
idiomatic: "Xun now means to defy his father, abandon his rank, and seize the north at Heng and Shuo."

literal: Under Heaven there has never been a state without a father; how deep is his concealment—heart and body together.
idiomatic: "There is no realm without a father. How deep is his treachery—heart and deed as one."

literal: If this boy today is not destroyed he is the great calamity of the state; if we wait until I have no successor, I fear there will be chaos like that of Yongjia.
idiomatic: "If I do not destroy this boy today, he will be the state's great ruin. If I wait until I have no heir left, I fear another Yongjia upheaval."

literal: " Thereupon he was deposed to commoner rank, placed at Heyang, guarded by soldiers; food and clothing supplied barely kept off hunger and cold.
idiomatic: He was deposed to commoner rank and sent to Heyang under guard. Food and clothing were given only enough to keep hunger and cold at bay.

literal: Xun in his straits came somewhat to know fault and repentance; he constantly read Buddhist sutras, bowed, and turned his heart toward good.
idiomatic: In his fall Xun came partly to repent. He read Buddhist sutras, bowed, and turned his heart toward what was good.

literal: When Gaozu visited Dai he then proceeded to Chang'an.
idiomatic: When Gaozu went to Dai he continued on to Chang'an.

literal: The commandant of palace guards Li Biao seized an interval with a secret memorial reporting that Xun again plotted rebellion with his attendants.
idiomatic: Commandant of palace guards Li Biao sent a secret memorial reporting that Xun was again plotting rebellion with his attendants.

literal: Gaozu at Chang'an sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Xing Luan with the Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict and carrying peppered wine to Heyang, and bestowed death on Xun; he was then fifteen.
idiomatic: At Chang'an Gaozu sent palace secretariat attendant Xing Luan with the Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict and peppered wine to Heyang, and had Xun put to death. He was fifteen.

literal: He was enfolded in a coarse coffin in common dress and buried in Heyang city.
idiomatic: He was laid in a plain coffin in ordinary dress and buried in Heyang.

literal: In the winter of year twenty-two the reviewing censor's clerk Long Wenguan, sentenced to death for violating the law, reported to the Court Commander that when Xun before was seized by his attendants he had written by hand a plea that he did not know the circumstances, yet Li Biao the commandant and attendant censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report upward.
idiomatic: In the winter of year 22 the reviewing censor's clerk Long Wenguan, condemned to death for a legal offense, told the Court Commander that when Xun was seized his attendants had found a handwritten plea that he did not know what was afoot, yet Commandant Li Biao and attendant censor Jia Shang had buried the matter and never reported it.

literal: Jia was sentenced and imprisoned at the Court Commander.
idiomatic: Jia was sentenced and held at the Court Commander's office.

literal: At that time Biao had been dismissed and returned home; Gaozu was at Ye; the Director of Documents memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; they met an amnesty, and therefore the matter was not pursued to the end.
idiomatic: By then Biao had been dismissed and gone home. Gaozu was at Ye. The secretariat memorialized to arrest Biao and send him to Luoyang, but an amnesty intervened and the case was never pursued to its roots.

literal: Jia Shang was released from prison; sudden illness; within several days he died.
idiomatic: Jia Shang was released from prison, fell suddenly ill, and died within days.

literal: Initially Gaozu was to marry Xun to Minister of Works Feng Dan's eldest daughter; because the girl was young he waited until she came of age.
idiomatic: At first Gaozu meant to marry Xun to the eldest daughter of Minister of Works Feng Dan, but because the girl was young he waited until she grew.

literal: First he betrothed for him the daughters of Pengcheng Liu Changwen and Xingyang Zheng Yi as left and right Ruzi; at the time Xun was thirteen or fourteen.
idiomatic: He first betrothed to him the daughters of Liu Changwen of Pengcheng and Zheng Yi of Xingyang as left and right concubines when Xun was thirteen or fourteen.

literal: Gaozu floated a boat on the Tianyuan Pool and said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian: "In life one must let oneself go; one cannot read books from morning to night.
idiomatic: Gaozu drifted a boat on the Tianyuan Pool and said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian, "A man must sometimes loosen the rein. He cannot read from dawn to dusk."

literal: I wish to have Xun go out in the morning to review the classics, return within after eating, go out again at the hour of shen, and stop at dusk.
idiomatic: "I mean to have Xun go out each morning to study the classics, return at midday, go out again in the afternoon, and be done by evening."

literal: You all take it how?
idiomatic: What do you think?"

literal: " Guang said: "Confucius said: 'When the blood and breath are not yet settled, beware of color'; the tradition says: 'By day inquire into affairs, by night rest the body.'
idiomatic: Cui Guang said, "Confucius warned, 'When blood and breath are unsettled, beware of desire.' The tradition says, 'By day attend to affairs; by night rest the body.'"

literal: The crown prince, in the years when he first touches learning, should not in the bright hours of day set aside his books and enter the inner quarters; this also is not how to settle a tender body and secure years of life.
idiomatic: "The crown prince is still in his first years of study. He should not in broad daylight leave his books for the inner quarters—that is no way to guard a tender frame or secure a long life."

literal: " Gaozu took Guang's words as right and therefore did not let Xun enter within by day.
idiomatic: Gaozu accepted Guang's counsel and would not let Xun enter the inner palace by day.

literal: He had no sons.
idiomatic: He left no sons.

literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande.
idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Jingzhao, styled Xuande.

literal: Enfeoffed in Taihe year twenty-one.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 21.

literal: He was appointed commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou; Pengcheng Wang's center-army office chief clerk Lu Yangwu was made acting chief clerk, and great and small matters of the province were entrusted to Yangwu.
idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou. Lu Yangwu, chief clerk of the Prince of Pengcheng's center-army office, served as acting chief clerk, and every detail of the province was left to him.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made guardian general of the army.
idiomatic: At the start of Shizong's reign he was made guardian general of the army.

literal: Shizong cherished his younger brothers; Yu and the others constantly went in and out of the palace women's quarters, morning and evening sleeping and dwelling as if a family household.
idiomatic: Shizong doted on his younger brothers. Yu and the others moved freely through the palace quarters, sleeping and waking with him morning and evening like members of one household.

literal: Each day Shizong shot for sport in the Hualin Garden; in light dress and mounted retinue they came and went without interval.
idiomatic: Every day Shizong shot for sport in the Hualin Garden, and Yu rode with him in light dress, back and forth without pause.

literal: Transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the secretariat.

literal: Shizong married for him the younger sister of Empress Shun as consort, but Yu did not treat her with ritual courtesy.
idiomatic: Shizong gave him the younger sister of Empress Shun as consort, but Yu never showed her proper courtesy.

literal: While Yu was in Xuzhou he took a concubine, Lady Li, originally surnamed Yang, a man of Dong commandery; hearing her sing at night he was pleased and thereafter she received his favor.
idiomatic: While Yu held Xuzhou he took a concubine, Lady Li—born Yang, from Dong commandery. He heard her sing one night, was delighted, and thereafter she held his favor.

literal: When he left the province and returned to the capital he wished to advance her rank; he entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery to act as her adoptive father, and by that rite married her; she bore the son Baoyue.
idiomatic: When he left office for the capital he wished to raise her standing. He had Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery stand as her adoptive father, married her by that rite, and she bore Baoyue.

literal: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace, beat and reviled her, forced her to become a nun within, and gave the child to the consort to rear.
idiomatic: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace, struck and abused her, forced her to take the tonsure inside, and gave the child to the consort to raise.

literal: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long had borne no child, submitted a memorial urging that secondary consorts attend the bed.
idiomatic: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, seeing that she still bore no child, memorialized urging that secondary consorts attend the bed.

literal: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love grew still stronger.
idiomatic: The empress was made to return Li to Yu, and his old love burned hotter than before.

literal: Yu loved literary composition and notably composed poetry and fu.
idiomatic: Yu loved letters and wrote poetry and fu with some distinction.

literal: At the time he constantly drew in talented men Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others to share feasts and joy; he recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four directions such as Yan Huaizhen, housed them, and honored them with ritual.
idiomatic: He often gathered men of talent—Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others—for feasts and delight, and hosted several dozen Confucian guests from across the realm, including Yan Huaizhen, treating them with full ceremony.

literal: The grain and silk he received he mostly dispersed in gifts.
idiomatic: Most of the grain and silk that came to him he gave away.

literal: He also revered the Buddhist way; his expenses often fell short.
idiomatic: He also devoted himself to Buddhism, and his expenses often outran his income.

literal: With his younger brother the Prince of Guangping Huai he rather vied in display, emulating extravagant splendor, greedy and lawless.
idiomatic: With his younger brother Huai, Prince of Guangping, he vied in display, each chasing extravagance, greedy and heedless of law.

literal: Thereupon Shizong took Yu into the forbidden precinct to investigate, caned him fifty times, and sent him out as governor of Ji.
idiomatic: Shizong then had Yu seized in the inner palace, investigated him, gave him fifty strokes, and sent him out as governor of Ji.

literal: At first Yu himself thought that by his office he might obtain attendance on important affairs; [5] now that his power was inferior to his two younger brothers he secretly harbored shame and resentment and rather showed it in speech and countenance.
idiomatic: At first Yu had believed his rank would win him a place near power; [5] finding himself weaker than his two younger brothers, he nursed secret shame and let it show in word and face.

literal: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, within and without he was estranged and suppressed.
idiomatic: His favored concubine had been shamed again and again, and at court and at home he was isolated and pressed down.

literal: When in the province he plotted rebellion, Yu then killed chief clerk Yang Lingyin and marshal Li Zun, claiming to have received a secret letter from the Prince of Qinghe saying Gao Zhao plotted to murder the sovereign.
idiomatic: While he was in the province he rose in rebellion. Yu killed chief clerk Yang Lingyin and marshal Li Zun, claiming a secret letter from the Prince of Qinghe that Gao Zhao meant to murder the emperor.

literal: Thereupon he made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial title.
idiomatic: He built an altar south of Xindu, burned offerings and declared himself to Heaven, and took the imperial title on the spot.

literal: He proclaimed amnesty for all under Heaven, era name Jianping year one, and installed Lady Li as empress.
idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Jianping year 1, and made Lady Li empress.

literal: Shizong ordered Director of Documents Li Ping to campaign against Yu.
idiomatic: Shizong ordered Director of Documents Li Ping to suppress Yu.

literal: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then closed the city and held it.
idiomatic: Yu marched out against the imperial host, was beaten again and again, and finally shut himself in the city.

literal: Yu knew the affair was exhausted; he took Li and four sons with several tens of horsemen and went out the gate; the armies pursued and seized him and sent him in.
idiomatic: Seeing all was lost, Yu took Li and four sons and rode out with a few dozen horsemen. The armies overtook him, seized him, and sent him in.

literal: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with the teaching of a family.
idiomatic: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him as kin.

literal: Whenever Yu halted at a post station he always took Li by the hand and indulged their private feeling to the full.
idiomatic: At every post station Yu held Li by the hand and gave their private bond its full expression.

literal: Though in fetters, in eating and drinking he was as before, with scarcely a shade of shame or fear.
idiomatic: Even in chains he ate and drank as before, showing hardly a trace of shame or fear.

literal: When he reached Yewang Yu said to others: "Though the sovereign's kindness is deep and he will not bear to kill me, what face have I to see the August One!"
idiomatic: At Yewang Yu told those about him, "The emperor's mercy runs deep and he may spare my life—but what face have I left to show the throne?"

literal: " Thereupon he sobbed, tears flowing; his breath broke and he died; he was then twenty-one.
idiomatic: He wept until his breath failed and he died. He was twenty-one.

literal: Some say Gao Zhao had men kill him.
idiomatic: Some said Gao Zhao had him killed.

literal: He was enfolded in a small coffin and buried.
idiomatic: He was laid in a small coffin and buried.

literal: When the sons reached Luoyang they were all pardoned.
idiomatic: When his sons reached Luoyang they were all pardoned.

literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling ordered that Yu's four sons all be entered on the register of kin, and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.
idiomatic: Later Empress Dowager Ling had Yu's four sons entered on the clan register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.

literal: The son Baoyue inherited.
idiomatic: His son Baoyue inherited the title.

literal: He then reburied his parents and observed mourning for three years.
idiomatic: He reburied his parents and observed three years of mourning.

literal: Baoyue's younger brother Baoju was frivolous and of slight conduct, addicted to wine and women.
idiomatic: Baoyue's younger brother Baoju was rash and loose in conduct, given to wine and women.

literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaozhuang he was specially enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he was specially enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.

literal: He followed the Deposed Emperor out and perished west of the Pass.
idiomatic: He followed the Deposed Emperor west of the Pass and perished there.
